questions.q: At the start of the chapter, how did Buck behave toward Spitz?
choices: He picked fights with Spitz every single evening in camp
He was patient and avoided fights whenever he could
He tried hard to make friends with Spitz by sharing food
He stayed close to Francois so Spitz could never reach him
questions.evidence: he avoided them whenever possible

questions.q: What made Buck finally spring at Spitz at the camp on Lake Le Barge?
choices: Spitz had taken over Buck's warm nest under the rock
Spitz had eaten Buck's fish while he was away
Spitz had bitten Billee while the men were asleep
Spitz had tangled Buck's traces on purpose during the day's run
questions.evidence: he found his nest occupied

questions.q: Why was Spitz so surprised when Buck attacked him that night?
choices: He had always thought of Buck as an unusually timid dog
He thought Francois had already tied Buck up for the night
He believed Buck was too tired from the long day's run
He did not know that Buck had seen him take the nest
questions.evidence: his rival was an unusually timid dog

questions.q: What interrupted the first fight between Buck and Spitz?
choices: Perrault fired his rifle into the air to frighten them
The ice of the lake broke and they fell into the water
A crowd of starving huskies crept into the camp
Francois pulled them apart and tied them to the sled
questions.evidence: The camp was suddenly discovered to be alive with skulking furry forms

questions.q: What did the starving huskies want when they came into the camp?
choices: To drive the team-dogs away from their warm hunting grounds
To find a new leader for their pack among the team-dogs
The food, which had made them crazed with hunger
To get warm by the men's driftwood fire on the lake ice
questions.evidence: They were crazed by the smell of the food.

questions.q: Besides food, what did the starving huskies eat in the camp?
choices: Perrault's moose-hide moccasins and part of Francois's whip
Every one of the letters Perrault was carrying
The canvas tent the men had brought from Dyea
Every one of the dog harnesses, so that new ones had to be bought
questions.evidence: They had eaten a pair of Perrault's moose-hide moccasins

questions.q: Why was crossing the Thirty Mile River so dangerous?
choices: The river was full of rocks that broke the runners
The water was wide open and the ice held only in quiet places
Hungry wolves followed the team closely along both banks of the river
Deep snow had buried the trail and hidden the cliffs
questions.evidence: The Thirty Mile River was wide open.

questions.q: How did Perrault keep from going under when he broke through the ice?
choices: He held a long pole that fell across the hole
He tied a rope from his belt to the loaded sled
He wore snowshoes that spread out his weight
He jumped back before the ice gave way under him
questions.evidence: being saved by the long pole he carried

questions.q: "Nothing daunted him. It was because nothing daunted him that he had been chosen for government courier." What does "daunted" mean?
choices: Made him tired and sleepy
Made him laugh or joke
Made him afraid or discouraged
Made him angry with the dogs
questions.evidence: Nothing daunted him.

questions.q: When the rim ice broke away before and behind them, how did the team escape?
choices: They waded across to the far bank in shallow water
They were hoisted one by one up the cliff with a rope
They waited on a block of ice until it drifted ashore
They broke a path through the ice with Perrault's axe
questions.evidence: the dogs were hoisted, one by one, to the cliff crest

questions.q: What did Francois do to help Buck when his feet became sore?
choices: He let Buck ride on top of the sled for several days
He wrapped Buck's feet in strips torn from his blanket
He made four moccasins for Buck from his own moccasins
He gave Buck an extra ration of fish every night
questions.evidence: sacrificed the tops of his own moccasins to make four moccasins for Buck

questions.q: Why did Perrault grin one morning at Buck?
choices: Buck lay on his back waving his feet, refusing to go without his moccasins
Buck had stolen Perrault's whole breakfast right out of the hot frying pan by the fire
Buck had pulled the whole loaded sled up a hill all by himself
Buck had dug himself so deep in the snow nobody could find him
questions.evidence: his four feet waving appealingly in the air

questions.q: What did Spitz do right after Francois saved Buck from Dolly?
choices: He helped drive the other dogs away from Buck
He attacked Buck while Buck was too exhausted to fight
He ran off into the woods and hid until night
He took Buck's place in the traces behind Dave
questions.evidence: This was Spitz's opportunity.

questions.q: Why did Spitz see Buck as a danger to him?
choices: Buck was the only dog Perrault would let near the sled
Buck was a Southland dog who endured and threatened his leadership
Buck had already beaten Spitz badly in a fight back on the beach at Dyea
Buck was much faster than Spitz at the head of the team
questions.evidence: felt his supremacy threatened by this strange Southland dog

questions.q: What did Buck do when Spitz went to punish Pike for hiding?
choices: He helped Spitz drag Pike out of his hiding place
He flew in between them and knocked Spitz off his feet
He barked loudly to warn Francois about the fight
He hid in the snow himself so Spitz would not see him
questions.evidence: Buck flew, with equal rage, in between

questions.q: After Francois whipped him for helping Pike, how did Buck keep stirring up trouble?
choices: He did it slyly, when Francois was not around
He did it only at night while the men were asleep
He stopped completely and obeyed Spitz from then on
He got Dave and Sol-leks to fight Spitz for him
questions.evidence: he did it craftily, when Francois was not around

questions.q: "With the covert mutiny of Buck, a general insubordination sprang up." What does "insubordination" mean?
choices: Being very sick and weak
Running away into the woods
Refusing to obey the leader
Working harder than before
questions.evidence: a general insubordination sprang up

questions.q: In Dawson, what did Buck love to join in every night?
choices: The races down the main street with the other teams
The weird and eerie song of the huskies
The hunt for rabbits along the frozen creeks
The fights between the miners' dogs by the saloon
questions.evidence: a weird and eerie chant, in which it was Buck's delight to join

questions.q: What began the chase that led to the final fight between Buck and Spitz?
choices: Dub turned up a snowshoe rabbit and missed it
A moose wandered close to the police dogs' camp
Spitz stole a fish and ran off across the river
A wolf howled from the nearby hills
questions.evidence: Dub turned up a snowshoe rabbit, blundered it, and missed

questions.q: What quality helped Buck win against Spitz, the practised fighter?
choices: His greater weight, which let him knock Spitz over easily
His imagination, which let him fight with his head as well
Francois's help, since he drove the other dogs away
His speed, which let him outrun Spitz on the creek
questions.evidence: But Buck possessed a quality that made for greatness--imagination.
